comparisons.peer_topic: Stock Repurchase Program Activity and Status
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's authorized $12 billion stock repurchase program saw the company repurchase 5.9 million shares for $862 million during the fiscal year ended December 28, 2024, with $4.7 billion remaining as of that date. The program has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time without obligation to acquire any specific amount of stock.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom disclose their stock repurchase program activity for fiscal year 2024, including shares repurchased and amounts spent. However, they differ significantly in program structure and remaining capacity. Broadcom's specific $20 billion program (authorized in 2021/2022) was fully utilized prior to expiration in 2023, and the company spent $7,176 million in 2024, implying reliance on newer or unspecified authority for that specific fiscal year spend. In contrast, AMD operates an open-ended $12 billion program with no termination date, spending $862 million in 2024 while retaining $4.7 billion in remaining authorization. Broadcom's disclosure highlights the completion of a fixed-term program, whereas AMD's highlights ongoing availability.

sentences.text: During fiscal years 2024, 2023 and 2022, we repurchased and retired approximately 67 million, 91 million and 117 million shares of our common stock for $7,176 million, $5,824 million and $7,000 million, respectively.
All $20 billion of the authorized amount under these stock repurchase programs was utilized prior to expiration on December 31, 2023.
During the year ended December 28, 2024, the Company repurchased 5.9 million shares of its common stock under the Repurchase Program for $862 million.
As of December 28, 2024, $4.7 billion remained available for future stock repurchases under this program.
This Repurchase Program does not obligate the Company to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.

comparisons.comparison: Micronix (MU) and Broadcom both report stock repurchase activities in fiscal year 2024 under discretionary programs. Broadcom repurchased approximately 67 million shares for $7,176 million in 2024, while Micron repurchased 3.2 million shares for $300 million in 2024. A key similarity is that both companies explicitly state their repurchase programs do not obligate them to acquire any specific amount of stock. A key difference is the program structure: Broadcom's reported activity relates to the culmination of prior fixed-term $20 billion authorizations (expired 2023), whereas Micron's $10 billion authorization has no expiration date. Additionally, the scale of repurchases differed, with Broadcom's 2024 spend ($7.2B) being significantly higher than Micron's ($300M).

sentences.text: During fiscal years 2024, 2023 and 2022, we repurchased and retired approximately 67 million, 91 million and 117 million shares of our common stock for $7,176 million, $5,824 million and $7,000 million, respectively.
All $20 billion of the authorized amount under these stock repurchase programs was utilized prior to expiration on December 31, 2023.

The repurchase authorization has no expiration date, does not obligate us to acquire any common stock, and is subject to market conditions and our ongoing determination of the best use of available cash.
We repurchased 3.2 million shares of our common stock for $300 million in 2024 and 8.6 million shares for $425 million in 2023.
